correctness.rationale: The Gaussian-normalized support representation is exact. A uniform rank permutation makes the collision event combinatorial. For k proportional to sqrt(N), rare row/column-conflicting rank pairs form a marked Poisson process: factorial moments for disjoint pairs supply intensity 2c^2 du dv and overlap components of at least three ranks have vanishing total contribution O(k^3/N^2). On the high-probability disjoint-pair event, omitted weaker scores give a lower bound; replacing them with the next tight number of ranked cells gives an upper bound whose Gaussian-quantile scaled discrepancy vanishes. The weak-rank mark v has density 2v, so its loss -log v is exponential of rate two. Upper and lower ranked coordinate lists couple to independent samples with error O(k^2/N^2); projected-Gaussian norm concentration handles intrinsic sphere. The atom at zero is proved separately from collision counts, not incorrectly inferred by continuity. A replayable optimizer checker supplies 225 exact small comparisons and 1211 conditional sandwich checks; simulations are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary work gives facet, optimization, diameter, and normality properties of the polytope, not a Gaussian intrinsic spherical width-loss law compared with a hypersimplex. Earlier partial random assignment literature concerns minimum exponential costs, with different distributional and scaling questions. Indexed geometry findings for related fixed-cardinality matching polytopes concern John or Lowner ellipsoids, incenters, and one-skeleton degrees. None of the inspected statements or indexed summaries implies the proposed critical-rank compound-Poisson law; this is qualified originality, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed probabilistic matching papers could express the same critical-rank compound-Poisson law in a nongraphical formulation.
Complete full-text comparison of the two older random-assignment articles was not available; their abstracted distributional questions are different but cannot exclude every subsidiary lemma.
The claim concerns an exact Gaussian model: alternative score-tail distributions may require a different scaling and were not treated.

value.rationale: The gap is intrinsic to nested natural polytopes: how a matching constraint alters a random support plane and the associated width of the containing cardinality hypersimplex. The first nontrivial regime is a square-root-rank threshold, and the theorem gives not just collision probability but the full non-Gaussian loss-size law with a characteristic Poisson count and exponential correction. This quantified boundary is relevant to the geometry of normal-fan agreement and to random linear optimization, and it is not a mere reparameterization of the earlier known ellipsoid or matching-face formulas.
